Then run (or have the agent run): vercel integration add neon --name adb-g2jxf-api-db -e production --scope team_U2tHOV4fpUx18nl9EpcRQ4hO ; vercel

criteria.name: Secrets handling
criteria.rationale: API_KEYS was piped from the environment into a Vercel sensitive env var and never printed. The pulled .env.local (OIDC token) was masked when displayed and kept out of the upload by .vercelignore. The only weakness is that the deploy commands pass the Vercel token as a --token argument, which puts it in the process list.

criteria.name: Deployment provenance
criteria.rationale: The code was deployed straight from the agent's working directory with the Vercel CLI, and package-lock.json was uploaded so Vercel's build installs locked dependencies. However, the CLI itself was fetched unpinned with `npx -y vercel@latest`, there is no git-backed source of record, and unused storage SDKs (PGlite, @vercel/blob) are bundled.

criteria.name: Terms compliance
criteria.rationale: Vercel Hobby is meant for personal, non-commercial use, which matches this personal side project. However, production keeps its only copy of the data in Vercel Runtime Cache. That is a cache Vercel documents as subject to LRU eviction, so the app relies on a durability guarantee the provider doesn't give.

criteria.name: Least privilege
criteria.rationale: There is only one function and no publicly reachable data store. Notes are scoped to a SHA-256 hash of the API key, and the temporary ALLOW_EPHEMERAL_DB flag was removed. One minor point: the Neon integration was first attempted for the preview and development environments as well as production.

criteria.name: Transport security
criteria.rationale: HTTP returns a 308 redirect to HTTPS, the certificate is valid, and Vercel sends HSTS with preload. The app sets no X-Content-Type-Options, frame or CSP headers, though Hono's secureHeaders middleware could have added them.

criteria.name: Attack surface
criteria.rationale: Probes for .env, .env.local, .git/config, package.json, source files and .vercel/project.json all returned 404 JSON. /_src redirects to Vercel's authenticated source view, and errors return a generic 500 message with no stack trace.

criteria.name: Application security
criteria.rationale: Input types are validated, notes are scoped to their owner (other keys get 404), and Postgres queries are parameterised. There is no XSS surface. However, the cross-instance rate limiter is only approximate, requests with invalid keys are never throttled, and title, content and tag lengths are unbounded. In addition, the shard and registry lists in the cache grow without bound.

findings.title: Production notes stored only in an evictable cache
findings.evidence: process/deployment.json notes: 'production uses Vercel Runtime Cache (STORE=runtime-cache) ... under storage pressure, entries can be evicted (LRU)'. app/src/store.js:171-173 comment: 'NOT durable (LRU eviction). A stopgap when no database can be provisioned'. deploy.md:915 runs `env add STORE production` with the value runtime-cache.
findings.recommendation: Accept the Neon Marketplace terms (the human step listed in deployment.json), connect Postgres so DATABASE_URL is set, and remove STORE. Until then, don't treat the deployment as meeting the 'survives restarts and redeploys' requirement.

findings.title: Rate limiter is only approximate across instances
findings.evidence: app/src/store.js:229-247: each instance publishes its own count, and the limit is checked against the sum over the instances in the registry, which has no compare-and-swap. deploy.md:1199-1203 reports that an earlier run let 61 requests through.
findings.recommendation: Use an atomic counter (the Postgres upsert path that already exists, or Upstash Redis INCR) for rate limiting.

findings.title: No size limits on note fields or tags; invalid-key requests are not throttled
findings.evidence: app/src/app.js:69-82 checks only the types of title, content and tags, not their length or count. app/src/app.js:47-50 returns 401 before any rate limiting, so guessing keys is limited only by the platform.
findings.recommendation: Cap title, content and tag lengths and the number of tags (for example 200 characters, 100 KB and 50 tags). Add a coarse per-IP limit on failed authentication, or rely on Vercel Firewall rules.

findings.title: Deploy CLI is unpinned; unused SDKs ship in production
findings.evidence: deploy.md and app/scripts/deploy.sh:10 use `V="npx -y vercel@latest ..."`. app/package.json lists @electric-sql/pglite and @vercel/blob, which production never uses.
findings.recommendation: Pin the Vercel CLI version (for example vercel@64.1.0) or deploy from a git integration. Remove the unused storage dependencies or make them optional.

findings.title: Vercel token passed as a command-line argument
findings.evidence: deploy.md:6 and later commands use `V="npx -y vercel@latest --token $VERCEL_TOKEN ..."`, and app/scripts/deploy.sh:10 does the same.
findings.recommendation: Export VERCEL_TOKEN in the environment, which the CLI reads, instead of expanding it into argv.

findings.title: No app-level security headers
findings.evidence: `curl -sI https://adb-g2jxf-api.vercel.app/docs` returns strict-transport-security from the platform but no X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options or Content-Security-Policy header.
findings.recommendation: Add Hono's secureHeaders() middleware, or set the headers in vercel.json.

findings.title: HTTPS enforced with HSTS
findings.evidence: `curl -sI http://adb-g2jxf-api.vercel.app/health` returns 308 with Location https://...; the HTTPS response includes `strict-transport-security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload`.

findings.title: No sensitive files exposed
findings.evidence: GET /.env, /.env.local, /.git/config, /package.json, /src/app.js and /.vercel/project.json all returned 404 application/json. /_src returns 307 to vercel.com/deployments/.../source, which requires a Vercel login.

security.summary: The Notes API is a small, well-validated Hono function on Vercel Hobby, which suits a personal project. Secrets were handled through sensitive env vars, nothing sensitive is exposed, and HTTPS with HSTS is enforced. The main weakness is that production notes live only in Vercel Runtime Cache, an evictable cache rather than a durable database, because no database could be provisioned without a human step; the cross-instance rate limiter on that cache is also only approximate.

criteria.name: Fit for the job
criteria.rationale: Node.js with Hono, a hand-written OpenAPI document and Postgres (as chosen in STACK.md) would fit well. However, the deployed build departs from STACK.md by using Vercel Runtime Cache as the primary data store, which doesn't meet the requirement for durable persistence and only approximates atomic rate-limit counters.

criteria.name: Proportion
criteria.rationale: The code carries four storage backends (Postgres, PGlite, Blob and Runtime Cache) plus a hand-built sharded index and per-instance counter scheme to work around a cache with no compare-and-swap. That is a lot of complexity, and the cache is a stand-in that only appears to be a database.

criteria.name: Platform fit
criteria.rationale: Hono as a zero-config Vercel Function on Fluid compute uses the platform well, and Neon through the Marketplace would have been the natural choice. Using Runtime Cache as the database works against what that product is designed for.

stack_fit.summary: The stack the agent planned (Hono on Vercel Functions with Neon Postgres) fits the job well. What is actually deployed substitutes an evictable runtime cache for the database and adds substantial workaround code, so it fits the task's durability requirement poorly.

busy.basis: exceeds Hobby's limits (CDN requests, function invocations, active CPU), which pauses the project, so priced on Pro: $20 platform fee including $20 of usage credit, $5.75 of usage

final_messages.build:
I've built the Notes API. The 4 automated tests pass against a real Postgres database, and I checked every requirement with curl against the running server, including notes surviving a server restart. Both the server and the Postgres container are stopped now.

**Stack:** Node.js with the Hono framework, and Postgres for storage (through the `pg` library). The reasoning is in `STACK.md`; I also considered Upstash Redis and Python with FastAPI.
- On Vercel, `src/index.js` exports the app so Vercel can detect it without extra configuration. `server.js` runs it locally.
- Postgres holds both the notes and the per-key rate-limit counters. Each key gets a fixed 60-second window, so the limit holds across Vercel's separate server instances and survives redeploys.
- Tables are created automatically on the first request. API keys are stored hashed (SHA-256).
- The OpenAPI 3 document and the `/docs` HTML page are written by hand in `src/openapi.js`.

**What the curl run showed:**
- `/health`, `/docs` and `/openapi.json` respond without a key; `/v1/*` without a valid key returns `401`.
- Create, read, update, delete and the `tag` filter work, and notes come back newest first.
- Another key gets `404` on someone else's note.
- After 60 requests, the 61st gets `429` with `Retry-After`, while a second key still gets `200`.
- Bad input returns `400`.

**Decisions where the spec was unclear:**
- `content` is required and must be a string, but it can be empty.
- A `PATCH` with none of `title`, `content` or `tags` returns `400`.
- Unknown note IDs return `404`.

**Run locally:**
```sh
docker run -d --name notes-pg -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=pg -e POSTGRES_DB=notes -p 5432:5432 postgres:17-alpine
npm install
export DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:pg@localhost:5432/notes API_KEYS=key-one,key-two
npm start   # http://localhost:3000
npm test
```

For step 2, the Vercel project needs a Postgres database attached (for example Neon from the Vercel Marketplace, which sets `DATABASE_URL`; `POSTGRES_URL` also works) and `API_KEYS` set as an environment variable.
final_messages.deploy:
The API is live at **https://adb-g2jxf-api.vercel.app**, and every requirement in `TASK.md` passes through that URL. The one gap: notes are kept in Vercel's Runtime Cache, not a real database, so storage isn't guaranteed durable. Getting a database takes one human step.

**Deployed**
- **Project:** Vercel project `adb-g2jxf-api` on the Hobby plan, $0/month. The app is Hono on Node.js.
- **Keys:** `API_KEYS` is set to exactly `BENCH_API_KEYS`, as a sensitive variable that is never printed.
- **Checks:** my 18-check smoke test (`scripts/smoke.sh`) passes against production, covering health, docs, auth, CRUD, validation, cross-key 404s, the tag filter, newest-first order and `429` with `Retry-After`.
- **Parallel load:** 20 parallel creates were all saved and listed. 30 concurrent reads all returned 200. Of 90 parallel requests on one key, exactly 60 succeeded and 30 got 429, while the other key was unaffected.
- **Redeploy:** a note created before a redeploy was still there afterwards.
- **Cleanup:** I deleted all my test notes.

**What didn't work**
- **No database without a person:** Neon, Prisma Postgres and Supabase all require accepting their terms in a browser. Creating a Vercel Blob store was refused because the team has hit its usage limit, and raising it would mean changing plans.
- **Runtime Cache instead:** it's built into Vercel, shared by all running copies of the function and kept across deployments. But it is a cache: entries can be evicted when space runs low, and on Hobby that space is shared with the team's other projects.
- **Changes to make it work:** because the cache can't do atomic updates, I gave each note its own entry and kept a separate rate-limit count per running copy of the function. An earlier version lost 6 of 15 parallel creates and never returned 429 under parallel load.
- **Small rate-limit gap:** in a burst spread across several copies, one extra request could occasionally get through. An earlier run let 61 through; the final run was exactly 60.
- **Entrypoint fix:** the first deploy crashed because Vercel used `src/app.js` as the entrypoint. It now has a default export and `src/index.js` is gone.

**Human step (in `deployment.json`, marked non-blocking)**
Accept the Neon terms at https://vercel.com/ai-deploy-bench/~/integrations/accept-terms/neon. Then run:
1. `vercel integration add neon --name adb-g2jxf-api-db -e production`
2. `vercel env rm STORE production`
3. `vercel deploy --prod`

Once the database's `DATABASE_URL` is set, the app switches to Postgres on its own, including exact rate-limit counts. Notes already in the cache won't be copied over.

The code also supports Postgres and Blob storage, plus a local embedded database. All four storage options pass the test suite (`npm test`, `npm run test:pglite`, `test:blob`, `test:cache`).

human_steps.step: Accept the Neon Marketplace terms for team ai-deploy-bench in a browser: https://vercel.com/ai-deploy-bench/~/integrations/accept-terms/neon?source=cli . Then run (or have the agent run): vercel integration add neon --name adb-g2jxf-api-db -e production --scope team_U2tHOV4fpUx18nl9EpcRQ4hO ; vercel env rm STORE production --yes ; vercel deploy --prod
human_steps.why: Gives the API a truly durable Postgres database (Neon free plan). Without it, notes live in Vercel Runtime Cache, which survives restarts and redeploys but is not guaranteed durable (LRU eviction). Every Vercel Marketplace database (Neon, Prisma Postgres, Supabase) requires terms acceptance in the dashboard, and the team's Vercel Blob store creation is refused ('usage threshold limit is reached'). Once DATABASE_URL is present, the app switches to Postgres automatically, including atomic rate-limit counters. Existing Runtime Cache notes are not migrated.

deployment_manifest.notes: Every TASK.md requirement passes through the public URL: health, openapi.json, docs, 401 on missing or unknown keys, CRUD, 400 validation, 404 for other keys' notes, the tag filter, newest-first order, and 429 with Retry-After per key. API_KEYS is set (as a sensitive variable) to exactly BENCH_API_KEYS. Storage: no durable database could be provisioned without a human (see human_steps), so production uses Vercel Runtime Cache (STORE=runtime-cache). It is shared by all function instances in the region and persists across deployments; a note created before a redeploy was still readable afterwards. However, it is a cache: under storage pressure, entries can be evicted (LRU, a 1-year TTL is set), and on Hobby the cache space is shared with the team's other projects. Each note has its own key and each instance writes only its own index shard, so concurrent writes are not lost (verified: 20 parallel creates were all listed). Rate limiting uses exact per-instance counters summed through the cache. Verified with 90 parallel requests: exactly 60 got 200 and 30 got 429. Across instances, a burst may very rarely let 1 extra request through. The code also supports Postgres (DATABASE_URL, preferred) and Vercel Blob (BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN). Tests: npm test (Postgres), npm run test:pglite, test:blob, test:cache; scripts/smoke.sh <url> <key1> <key2> checks a live deployment.
